The company is currently seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant that can write code, browse the web, control apps, and navigate devices on a user's behalf. Apple is working on agents that can plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs while coordinating specialized subagents along the way. The company's App Store has been dominated by AI agents, so it has introduced a new warning in the upcoming macOS 27.3 update that prompts users to reconsider granting third-party agents permission to control their Macs.

Google's Project Suncatcher program is a long-term moonshot that aims to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into solar power. Its satellites each have the computing capacity of roughly the scale of a data center rack. The mission on New Glenn will deploy satellites into a Sun-synchronous orbit, where they will be able to receive nearly continuous solar energy.

articles.headline: Spacecraft reaches Mercury on second-ever mission to enter its orbit
articles.blurb: The BepiColombo mission is now preparing to swing into orbit around Mercury. The joint European-Japanese space mission aims to help scientists understand how Mercury formed so close to the Sun, why it has a magnetic field, and what makes up the frozen ice under the planet's permanently shadowed craters. The spacecraft will separate into two orbiters in early December. The orbiters will maneuver to different polar orbits around the planet, and science operations will begin in April next year.

articles.headline: PostgreSQL 19 Released!

The release introduces the `REPACK (CONCURRENTLY)` command, which enables users to optimize tables for their current workload without disruption to ongoing operations. It also gives users better control over plan stability and query performance with the new pg_plan_advice extension. PostgreSQL 19 gives users new ways to manage their workloads without disruption and build applications that span multiple systems.

articles.headline: The most important number in AI
articles.blurb: The Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI) is a measure of AI progress developed by Epoch AI, a nonprofit research organization. It provides a single number that summarizes how well AI models do on benchmarks. It is designed to be continuously updatable, and researchers can use it to look at trends going back years and forecast things for future models. This post covers how the ECI is constructed, the challenges of benchmark selection, whether it makes sense to talk about 'model IQ', whether static benchmarks stay relevant as models get better, and much more.

Many deals die early in the process, so keeping the circle tight avoids spooking customers unnecessarily. Bankers and lawyers also cost more than most founders expect.

CUDA Graphs on default Inductor kernels already recovered about 98% of megakernel performance.

articles.headline: Wait for pull request events with GitHub CLI
articles.blurb: GitHub CLI's new gh event commands let scripts wait for reviews, pull request changes, and completed check suites instead of repeatedly polling. The commands require CLI 2.105.0 or later and access to the Event Streams preview through its waitlist.

articles.blurb: GitLab 19.6 introduces Rapid Diffs, a rewrite that renders merge request diffs on the server and streams them to the browser, cutting first file load time to about 1.5 seconds.

articles.headline: Kraken Parent Payward Acquires Tribe Capital to Enter Private Markets
articles.blurb: Payward, Kraken's parent, agreed to acquire Tribe Capital, a venture firm managing $2.7 billion chaired by Payward and Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi, with closing expected in Q1 2027 at an undisclosed price. The deal adds private-market investing to a vertical buildout that also includes the pending purchase of derivatives exchange Bitnomial, a $600 million acquisition of stablecoin payments firm Reap, and the buyout of Magic Labs' wallet business. Sethi's concurrent role as Tribe chair and Payward co-CEO positions the transaction as a formal consolidation of an already-integrated executive relationship rather than a standard external acquisition.

articles.headline: Ledger expands hardware hack investigation to Germany and UAE
articles.blurb: Ledger says new tampered devices in Berlin and Dubai are the same incident as the Southeast Asia campaign, with extra hardware that captures the recovery phrase during setup, and one case involves the newer Nano Gen5. It says there is no flaw in its chip or OS and no confirmed case from ledger.com. Two users claim a combined $604,000 in losses from a Dubai-authorized reseller, and Bitquery reports about $1.68M stolen from 16 wallets in Dubai and Berlin, after earlier claims of $102M from 335 wallets in Southeast Asia. Ledger has not confirmed loss amounts and expects more devices to surface.

articles.headline: Lightspark Launches Agent Accounts for AI Agents
articles.blurb: Lightspark announced Agent Accounts, dedicated financial accounts that give AI agents the ability to hold balances and transact autonomously across multiple payment rails and currencies. The product targets developers building agents that need native payment capabilities, positioning Lightspark's Lightning-based infrastructure as the broadest multi-method solution for agent-to-agent and agent-to-human payments.

articles.headline: Ant International launches protocol for real-time settlement
articles.blurb: The Whale Orchestration Protocol runs on Ant's WhaleRTP platform and enables delivery-versus-payment between tokenized deposits and tokenized money market funds, developed under MAS's BLOOM initiative. Pilots with DBS and Franklin Templeton are complete. Separately, MAS issued S$100M of tokenized MAS Bills on November 6, Standard Chartered expanded tokenized deposits across Singapore and Hong Kong, and StraitsX, OCBC, and Standard Chartered finished an interoperability trial.

articles.headline: The Everything-App Race: Stickiness, Rev-Sharing, and Cross-Margin
articles.blurb: Robinhood, Polymarket, Kalshi, Coinbase, Kraken, and Pump.fun are each expanding beyond their originating verticals, converging on a shared product surface spanning stocks, crypto spot, perps, prediction markets, and memecoins from divergent starting points across TradFi and crypto-native distribution. Three decisive factors: customer retention depth, rev-sharing structures that attract new users and retain whales, and cross-margin capability across the full product stack. No clear differentiation thesis has emerged.

articles.headline: Kalshi vs. Polymarket: Domain Experts Win
articles.blurb: Kalshi and Polymarket launched within months of each other, but Kalshi now posts roughly 4x the volume at 3x the valuation, with a $65B raise in talks versus Polymarket's unannounced $21B round. Kalshi's MIT math founders, with prior finance careers, sued the CFTC, won regulatory standing, then expanded into single-stock perps on 50+ companies, indices, and AI compute futures this year. Polymarket became a tab inside a memecoin application, sitting beside memecoins and perps, its standalone-exchange identity absorbed into a retail crypto product. Founder background drove the split: quant-finance founders built toward prediction markets as a regulated asset class, while operator-type founders built toward distribution as the product.

articles.headline: Why Bitcoin needs capital markets and how Stacks is building them
articles.blurb: Bitcoin lacks yield, credit, and trading markets, and holders shouldn't have to hand over BTC to earn. Stacks' Bitcoin staking is live, with bonds targeting 3% annual yield paid in BTC from miners' Proof of Transfer commitments. The first two bonds drew 735 BTC, with Bullish staking in Bond 3 and Anchorage offering custody. In 2027, Stacks plans an open auction through PoX-6 and borrowing stablecoins against staked BTC. STX is required at 5% of the BTC value, and SIP-034 raised block capacity up to 30x, with a 100x goal.

articles.headline: Morpho and Aave are in a full BD war
articles.blurb: Onchain lending now depends on distribution, partnerships, and integrations through neobanks, wallets, and exchanges, not just a good app. Morpho is plugging into apps people already use: Coinbase Borrow in New York, OKX Wallet on X Layer, earn products at Ledger, Bitso, Pulsar, Abra, and Deel, Robinhood Stock Tokens as collateral, and new APIs. Aave is pursuing infrastructure partners and new collateral through V4: Circle Mint, Privy, and Base for fintechs, Ethena Pay's Earn+, cirBTC, PAXGy, mWIN, and Coinbase tokenized stocks, plus the Avon acquisition for fixed-rate lending. V3 Core going blue-chip only pushes new assets to V4. The real race is owning tokenized non-crypto assets through early issuer partnerships, and most onchain lending will likely run on one of the two.

Microsoft will become the first company to use Intel Foundry's EMIB advanced packaging technology for its first-party silicon and secure multi-year Intel Xeon supply capacity, including the upcoming Diamond Rapids server CPUs. The partnership also covers system-level optimizations using CXL memory, Intel QuickAssist Technology, and Intel Trust Domain Extensions for confidential computing.

articles.blurb: Google Cloud's Jeanette Manfra argues that maintenance burdens and vendor lock-in are limiting organizations' AI ambitions. She cites Google-commissioned research in which 78% of surveyed technology leaders said maintaining legacy systems diverts resources from AI, and advocates greater vendor choice and stronger security requirements in procurement.

articles.headline: IT leaders are deciding which decisions machines can make on their own
articles.blurb: IT leaders and chief information officers are navigating the challenges of deploying autonomous IT and generative AI tools in high-security environments. While rules-based automation and large language models help synthesize large volumes of data and accelerate cybersecurity defenses, agencies face significant hurdles regarding data readiness, over-trust in AI results, and classifying sensitive information. Organizations are addressing these challenges by establishing localized large language models, data governance structures, and strict human-in-the-loop checkpoints.

articles.headline: Nvidia expands Azure infrastructure and on-premises AI options
articles.blurb: Nvidia and Microsoft are expanding access to Azure virtual machines powered by Vera Rubin systems and adding more model customization capabilities through Microsoft Foundry. Planned Azure Local support for additional Nvidia GPUs and Jetson platforms will extend deployment options to on-premises and industrial environments.

articles.headline: Introducing agent controls: An enterprise control plane for agent behavior
articles.blurb: Microsoft has introduced agent controls, a managed Azure service designed to help enterprises centrally define, manage, and evaluate policies governing AI agent behavior. Built on the open-source Agent Control Specification and Agent Hooks, the service brings runtime governance to heterogeneous AI agent fleets without requiring organizations to build custom policy infrastructure. It evaluates agent actions and content using content safety classifiers, LLM judges, and deterministic Rego rules.

The system separates bug finding from verification using parallel specialist sessions and per-bug deep checks. Data from seven months of production use on kernel mailing lists show that Sashiko completes about 1,200 reviews daily and correlates with a 35 percent drop in 60-day follow-up fixes for merged commits.

articles.blurb: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely, a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom, was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content.

Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet's access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices and karaoke machines.

articles.headline: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
articles.blurb: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.

articles.headline: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

articles.headline: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt

The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

But more than two years have passed since any sports stars graced the pitch. In 2024, as the surrounding city was almost entirely captured by heavily armed gangs, Sylvio Cator stadium – where football greats including Brazil’s Ronaldo and Roberto Carlos once played – also fell under criminal control, its dilapidated red and blue stands used as an outpost by fighters working for a gang boss called Izo. If I don’t eat it, they put the tube in me to feed me.” A Cuban asylum seeker, Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez, 32, said in messages to the Guardian this month that he was still weak and dizzy after three months without eating, but that he had broken his hunger strike because being force-fed was just too painful.

If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations. Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July.
